name: Tennis ball
headline: diameter
description: A tennis ball is a hollow rubber ball covered in fabric, usually bright yellow. The ITF Rules of Tennis require the standard fast and medium balls to measure 6.54 to 6.86 cm across and weigh 56.0 to 59.4 g. A larger, slower ball is also allowed, and every approved ball must pass bounce and squash tests too.

measures.label: Diameter
measures.note: Size limits for Type 1 (fast), Type 2 (medium) and high-altitude balls, 2.57-2.70 in

measures.label: Mass
measures.note: Mass limits for all ball types, 1.975-2.095 oz

facts.text: The Type 3 (slow) ball is larger, at 7.00-7.30 cm across, but has the same mass limits.
Dropped from a set height, a Type 1 (fast) ball must bounce back 138-151 cm.
The ITF checks a ball's size with two ring gauges: it must fall through the larger ring under its own weight but not through the smaller one.

sources.title: ITF Rules of Tennis 2026, Appendix I: The Ball

caveats: The Rules table calls this measure 'size'; the ITF's ball approval document explains it is the ball's diameter, checked with ring gauges.
The larger Type 3 (slow) ball, 7.00-7.30 cm, is not included in the headline range.
